title: Add a per-tier prompt-cache lifetime axis to the model catalog via the KDL rule tree
one_line: Add a rule-owned, per-tier numeric prompt-cache lifetime (short/long, in seconds) to the catalog as a new sibling KDL axis, without touching the existing OpenAI wire field.
user_visible_effect: none directly — internal. W7 adds no user-facing surface and changes no request bytes. It only makes a sourced per-tier TTL table expressible in the rule tree so that W8 (the default-off cache warmer) can read it instead of a hard-coded 5-minute constant. Shipping W7 without W8 changes nothing a user can observe.

steps.instruction: Above the `export interface AnthropicCompat` declaration, add two exported type aliases: `export type CacheRetentionTier = "short" | "long";` and `export type PromptCacheLifetime = Partial<Record<CacheRetentionTier, number>>;` with a doc comment stating the unit is SECONDS and that an absent key means that tier's lifetime is unknown. Place them near the other cache-related types (just before :526) rather than inside the interface.

Add `promptCacheLifetime?: PromptCacheLifetime;` to `AnthropicCompat` with a doc comment that says the value is rule-owned via the `prompt-cache-lifetime` KDL axis and is UNSET when the provider's cache behavior is unknown, so consumers must fail safe rather than default it. Do NOT add it to `OpenAICompat` (:237) — see C2.

`ResolvedAnthropicCompat` is `Required<Omit<AnthropicCompat, "streamIdleTimeoutMs" | "thinkingLoopGuard">> & {...}`. Because of the `Required<>`, a new optional field on `AnthropicCompat` becomes MANDATORY on the resolved type — which would contradict the fail-safe-absent contract. Add `"promptCacheLifetime"` to that `Omit<...>` union, then re-declare `promptCacheLifetime?: PromptCacheLifetime;` inside the `& { ... }` intersection, exactly as `streamIdleTimeoutMs` and `thinkingLoopGuard` are handled. This step is mandatory; skipping it makes the type lie about the runtime value.

In the AXES record, next to `"prompt-cache-maximum-checkpoints"` / `"prompt-cache-minimum-tokens"` / `"prompt-cache-mode"`, add `"prompt-cache-lifetime": wire("promptCacheLifetime", ["anthropic", "bedrock"], "object"),`. The third argument is the shape and MUST be `"object"` (a `scalar` axis takes exactly one positional arg and cannot carry a child block). Do not pass a `values` array — that vocabulary only applies to scalar/array shapes.

If the Bedrock consumers (packages/ai/src/providers/amazon-bedrock.ts:960) should read the same numbers, mirror the axis into the `on "amazon-bedrock"` block alongside the existing prompt-cache groups. If Bedrock keeps its existing boolean, skip this step and set the axis records to `["anthropic"]` only. Decide this with the open question OQ1 before writing either block.

Run `bun run gen:compat`. It must exit 0 and report the rule/class counts. Then `git status --short packages/catalog/` — the only expected changes are `rules.json` (plus `auth-ids.ts` / `provider-ids.ts` if they shift) and your `.kdl` edit. Commit the generated files together with the rule change, per AGENTS.md's Generated Files rule.

Write the rule test using synthetic `ModelSpec<"anthropic-messages">` objects (copy the `spec()` helper shape from anthropic-fable-5-1-cache-read.test.ts), so the assertions test the RULE and not the bundled JSON. Cover: (1) a model the KDL declares exposes BOTH tiers through `buildModel(...).compat.promptCacheLifetime`; (2) a model with no declaration resolves to `undefined` — assert this explicitly, do not let it pass by omission; (3) `buildModel` on the existing OpenAI gpt-5.6 fixtures still yields `promptCacheBreakpointTtl === "30m"` and `supportsPromptCacheBreakpoints === true`; (4) a negative case proving the axis does not leak onto a provider it was not authored for.

Write the wire-unchanged test. Build request params for an OpenAI Responses model WITH `promptCacheLifetime` set and one WITHOUT, and assert the resulting `prompt_cache_options` are deep-equal. For the responses path use the exported `buildParams` from packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses.ts:1174. For the completions path see OQ2 — its `buildParams` at :1797 is NOT exported, so you must choose an interception strategy first. Do not write this as a source-grep of the two `ttl:` lines; AGENTS.md bans asserting on implementation file text, and such a test would pass even if the axis were wired in backwards.

Add a one-line entry under `## [Unreleased]` in `packages/catalog/CHANGELOG.md` (and `packages/ai/CHANGELOG.md` if you touched packages/ai source). Keep it user-facing and brief — this is an internal capability with no user-visible effect, so phrase it as the capability it unlocks. Do not flag changelog section order in review; `bun run release` normalizes it.

test_contract: The observable contract is a negative one plus a containment guarantee. (a) A model the rule tree declares per-tier cache lifetimes for exposes BOTH tiers through `buildModel(...).compat.promptCacheLifetime` as numbers in seconds — a consumer reading the field learns the real TTL instead of guessing. (b) A model with no declaration resolves the field to `undefined`, asserted explicitly, so W8's fail-safe branch is defended rather than assumed; if the axis ever starts defaulting to 0 or to a hard-coded constant, this test goes red. (c) The pre-existing `promptCacheBreakpointTtl` still resolves to the literal `"30m"` for GPT-5.6+ on the official OpenAI API, proving the C3 decision (add a sibling axis, do not widen the existing wire field) was actually honored. (d) The `prompt_cache_options` object emitted for an OpenAI model that DOES declare `promptCacheLifetime` is deep-equal to the one emitted for an identical model that does NOT — so the new axis is provably inert on OpenAI traffic. If a future implementer widens `promptCacheBreakpointTtl` into a per-tier number, or lets the new axis leak into the OpenAI wire payload, (c) and (d) both fail. Consumers see no wire change and no cache-behavior change from this work item.

gate: All four must hold. (1) `bun run gen:compat` exits 0 and `git status --short packages/catalog/` shows only the expected regenerated files. (2) `bun run --filter @oh-my-pi/pi-catalog check:types` exits 0. (3) `bun run check:ts` introduces no NEW errors beyond the known concurrent-agent baseline (capture the baseline before you start — see risk). (4) Once the native addon is built, `bun test packages/catalog/test/prompt-cache-lifetime.test.ts packages/ai/test/prompt-cache-lifetime-wire-unchanged.test.ts` is green, and the pre-existing `packages/catalog/test/build.test.ts` "OpenAI explicit prompt-cache breakpoint compat" suite still passes unchanged. Gate (1) alone already catches the most likely wiring mistakes: an unregistered directive fails with `unknown directive \`prompt-cache-lifetime\``, a wrong shape fails with `directive ... has a malformed value`, and a camelCase child fails with `must be kebab-case`.
gate_can_fail: Yes, and it fails in a specific, diagnosable way. `gen:compat` is a real gate: `collectAxis`/`axisFor` in scripts/compat-compiler/compile-axes.ts throw CompatCompileError on an unknown directive, a scalar-shaped axis given a child block, a camelCase object child, or the same axis assigned twice in one block. The type gate is real: forgetting the `Omit` step makes `promptCacheLifetime` a required `PromptCacheLifetime` on `ResolvedAnthropicCompat` while `resolveAnthropicPolicy` never assigns it, which is a type error or a silent lie. HONEST CAVEAT, stated because it matters: the test half of this gate CANNOT RUN in this environment, so today only gates (1)-(3) are executable. And note explicitly that the compiler will NOT flag the 'two axes say the same thing' problem — see plan_corrections C6 — so gates (1)-(3) can all be green while the design decision is still unmade. That is why OQ1 is listed as a blocking open question rather than an implementation detail.
depends_on: HARD GATE, not a task: a sourced per-provider, per-tier prompt-cache TTL table must exist before this item starts (the plan's open question 0). The exact TTL numbers are the deliverable of that research; this item supplies the schema, not the data. An engineer who cannot source a number must leave the field undefined rather than guess — an over-estimated TTL causes refreshes to explode on an entry that would have survived; an under-estimated one only loses an occasional avoidable miss.
Nothing structural. Unlike most of this milestone, W7 does not depend on Wave 1 (W1/W2/W3/W5) — it touches no lifecycle or disposer code. It can be built in parallel with Wave 1.
W7 and W8 are intended to ship as one unit: the axis is dead weight alone, and the warmer is blocked without it.
blocks: W8 (the default-OFF Anthropic cache warmer) — blocked on the whole point of this axis. W8's current path hard-codes `ANTHROPIC_CACHE_TTL_MS = 5 * 60_000` at packages/ai/src/stream.ts:1209 and is switched on unconditionally at packages/coding-agent/src/sdk.ts:4111; W8 is the consumer that reads the new field.
effort: M — one KDL axis registration, two type-shape edits (one of which, the `Omit` list, is easy to miss), one or more sourced rule blocks, `gen:compat`, and two focused test files. The non-obvious cost is not the typing; it is sourcing defensible TTL numbers and deciding OQ1.
risk: The single most likely way to get this wrong is following the plan's file instruction literally — adding the field next to `promptCacheBreakpointTtl` at types.ts:403 — which puts it on `OpenAICompat`/`ResolvedOpenAISharedCompat` and makes the axis permanently invisible to the only consumer that needs it. `applyWireAxes` (resolve.ts:131-140) assigns a wire axis only when the model's API maps to one of the axis's declared records, and `API_COMPAT_RECORDS` maps `anthropic-messages` to `["anthropic"]` and `openai-responses` to `["openai-responses"]` — disjoint sets. An axis on the OpenAI records can never reach an Anthropic model, so the field would type-check, compile, regenerate cleanly, and still be dead at runtime. Second-most-likely: copying the `:258-266` anchor literally and landing the rule only inside `on "amazon-bedrock"`, which leaves first-party Anthropic — the family W8 actually warms — with no values. Neither mistake produces a red build.
open_questions: OQ1 (BLOCKING — the plan explicitly leaves this open, and it changes what you write in step 6). There is already a wired sibling axis, `supports-long-prompt-cache-retention` (axes.ts:153, records [...OAI, "bedrock"]), with two live consumers gating `ttl: "1h"` at packages/ai/src/providers/amazon-bedrock.ts:960 and packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses.ts:1253, resolved at resolve.ts:721 and :830 with a hard-coded `false` baseline at resolve.ts:899. It is declared at anthropic.kdl:266, 286, 292, 317, 328, 341, 349. Once `promptCacheLifetime` exists these are two sources of truth for the same fact. The plan's F5 block recommends (a) delete the boolean and migrate both consumers to `promptCacheLifetime?.long`, or (b) keep both with an explicit meaning split. Note that (a) is a breaking change touching two providers and a models.json regeneration, and is materially larger than this M-sized item. A human must pick. My recommendation: keep the boolean for this milestone (it is already shipped and correct), scope the new axis to `["anthropic"]` only, and file the consolidation as separate work — but that is a recommendation, not a decision I can make.

OQ2. The plan's test (4) requires building request params 'through the public path of the provider' for BOTH openai-responses.ts and openai-completions.ts. That is possible for responses (buildParams is exported at :1174 and calls the policy fn at :1365) but NOT for completions: its buildParams at :1797 is module-private, as is applyOpenAIChatCompletionsPromptCachePolicy at :1767, reachable only from :1999. Pick one: (a) export buildParams from openai-completions (a production change made purely for testability — cheapest, but widens public surface), (b) drive streamOpenAICompletions with an intercepted fetch (fully public, heavier, needs a mock server), or (c) cover responses via the exported buildParams and cover completions via a mock-fetch stream test. State the choice in the test file's header comment.

OQ3. Should `promptCacheLifetime` be user-overridable in `models.yml`? If yes it must also be added to the hand-maintained omptype schema at packages/coding-agent/src/config/models-config-schema-bundle.ts (NOT generated — it is hand-written; the sibling `supportsLongPromptCacheRetention?: "boolean"` appears at :70 and :96). If the axis is purely rule-owned, leave it out and say so. Default recommendation: leave it out, since AGENTS.md's ownership strata put this under the KDL tree.

plan_corrections.claim: (plan F5 block) 'The boolean axis doesn't set priority=, so resolve will throw AmbiguousOverlapError — you'll hit it at bun run gen:compat.'
plan_corrections.correction: `AmbiguousOverlapError` fires only when two EQUAL-RANK rules contest THE SAME axis key (cascade.ts:245-253 keys winners by axis; the class doc at cascade.ts:6-9 says rules resolve independently per axis). Two DIFFERENT axes never collide, and `collectAxis` errors only on a repeated assignment of the same key within one block. So authoring `prompt-cache-lifetime` alongside `supports-long-prompt-cache-retention` will NOT produce a compiler error. The two-sources-of-truth problem is real and AGENTS.md's spirit forbids it, but it is a design decision with no automated gate — which makes it MORE important to resolve deliberately (OQ1), not less. The plan promises a compiler tripwire that does not exist.
